questions.stem: A browser resolves the CLZ-330 profile. Where does its HTTP connection go?

options.A: Through a Traffic Manager HTTP proxy

optionExplanations.A: Traffic Manager does not proxy HTTP.
optionExplanations.B: Traffic Manager answers DNS; the endpoint receives application traffic.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform is not a client traffic relay.

questions.stem: Both endpoints are healthy. Which target should a fresh priority-routing DNS decision prefer?

optionExplanations.A: Priority 2 is the backup.
optionExplanations.C: Round robin is not configured.

questions.stem: The primary fails while the secondary stays healthy. What precedes health-based failover?

optionExplanations.A: Routing uses observed health.
optionExplanations.C: CLI installation does not control health.

questions.stem: Some clients reach the failed primary after the monitor detects failure. What explains this?

options.C: Cached DNS answers can outlive the health transition

optionExplanations.A: This lesson does not deploy a Load Balancer.
optionExplanations.B: No permanent user binding is provided.
optionExplanations.C: Resolver and client caching delays observed changes.

questions.stem: Which behavior satisfies this lesson's configured endpoint probe?

options.C: Healthy HTTPS response on port 443 at /

optionExplanations.A: SSH is the wrong protocol.
optionExplanations.C: The monitor explicitly uses HTTPS, 443, and /.
optionExplanations.D: SQL is unrelated to the monitor.

questions.stem: Which input format matches primary_endpoint_fqdn in CLZ-330?

options.A: Real public hostname without a scheme
options.B: Full https:// URL with a path

optionExplanations.A: The variable holds the endpoint host.
optionExplanations.B: A URL is not just a hostname.
optionExplanations.C: This pattern requires public endpoints.
optionExplanations.D: A resource group is not a DNS target.

questions.stem: A proposed target is reachable only inside a private VNet. Why is it unsuitable here?

options.C: Targets must share the profile's region
options.D: Public probes and Internet clients cannot reach that private-only target

optionExplanations.A: The OS is not the constraint.
optionExplanations.C: External endpoints need not share a region.
optionExplanations.D: This lesson assumes publicly reachable HTTPS services.

questions.stem: Both endpoint variables contain the same hostname. What should happen before applying?

options.A: Apply because two registrations provide redundancy
options.B: Stop and supply genuinely distinct services
options.C: Change only the endpoint resource label
options.D: Disable monitoring to hide the warning

optionExplanations.A: Both entries still reference one dependency.
optionExplanations.B: Two entries do not create independent services.
optionExplanations.C: The resource label does not change the target.
optionExplanations.D: That weakens monitoring without repairing redundancy.

questions.stem: The distinct_endpoints check assertion fails. What does that check block itself do?

options.A: Reports a warning without blocking the operation

optionExplanations.A: The learner must heed the warning and correct inputs.
optionExplanations.B: Checks are advisory, unlike blocking conditions.
optionExplanations.C: Checks do not rewrite variables.

questions.stem: DNS and probes work, but HTTPS to the trafficmanager.net profile fails certificate validation. What needs review?

options.C: Endpoint certificate and host configuration for the client-used hostname

optionExplanations.A: Location cannot fix a certificate name.
optionExplanations.C: DNS selection does not add certificate coverage.

questions.stem: Both endpoints show Online. What conclusion is justified?

options.B: Configured probes are healthy; real client-hostname requests still need testing

optionExplanations.A: Traffic Manager does not terminate client TLS.
optionExplanations.B: Probe success is narrower than end-to-end evidence.
optionExplanations.C: A simple probe cannot test every transaction.
optionExplanations.D: Monitoring does not inspect every cache.

questions.stem: An application needs a global reverse proxy, WAF, and managed TLS. Which comparison fits?

optionExplanations.A: Priorities cannot create a proxy.
optionExplanations.C: DNS records do not terminate TLS.

questions.stem: After CLZ-330 destroy, what happens to the independently hosted target applications?

options.C: They move to the profile's group

optionExplanations.A: DNS registration is not service ownership.
optionExplanations.C: No migration is configured.
optionExplanations.D: The lesson owns registrations, not application hosting.

questions.stem: The profile FQDN stays unchanged on no-change plans. What contributes to this?

options.B: Random suffix value retained in state

optionExplanations.A: DNS lookups do not run Terraform.
optionExplanations.C: Browser data does not own the resource.
optionExplanations.D: The suffix is a separate random resource.

questions.stem: Lost suffix state causes a profile replacement proposal. What should precede apply?

options.A: Apply because published names never matter
options.B: Overwrite the suffix directly in Azure
options.C: Review state recovery and consumer impact

optionExplanations.A: Hostnames can be part of consumer configuration.
optionExplanations.B: Manual edits do not recover Terraform ownership.
optionExplanations.C: Consumers may depend on the existing FQDN.

questions.stem: The profile has ttl=60. What does that control?

optionExplanations.A: TTL guides DNS caching.
optionExplanations.C: Initialization is unrelated.
optionExplanations.D: No VM reboot schedule is configured.

questions.stem: One target is Degraded. Which investigation follows this lesson?

options.B: Test its public HTTPS host, port, and path

optionExplanations.A: That reduces resilience.
optionExplanations.C: It does not diagnose the configured path.

questions.stem: Which exercise measures failover with a bounded service impact?

options.A: Stop the primary in a disposable test environment and observe health plus DNS timing

optionExplanations.A: Scoped nonproduction testing demonstrates the timing.
optionExplanations.C: No tenant-wide client-cache control exists.
optionExplanations.D: Removing both targets cannot prove successful failover.

questions.stem: One service is in Azure and one at another public provider. Can external endpoints represent both?

options.A: No, they must share an Azure region
options.B: Only after installing a Traffic Manager agent
options.D: Yes, if both satisfy public HTTPS requirements

optionExplanations.A: Their location is not constrained that way.
optionExplanations.C: The OS is not specified here.
optionExplanations.D: External targets can be outside Azure.

questions.stem: Which policy expresses a preferred primary plus backup service?

optionExplanations.A: Weighted expresses relative distribution.
optionExplanations.C: Priority gives ordered failover.

questions.stem: Why does the primary have priority 1 and secondary priority 2?

optionExplanations.A: The numbers order healthy targets.
optionExplanations.C: That confuses priority with weights.

questions.stem: Beyond profile queries and health checks, what cost should the estimate include?

options.A: One mandatory VM per DNS client

optionExplanations.A: Traffic Manager deploys no client VMs.
optionExplanations.B: DNS replies do not license Terraform.
optionExplanations.C: The lesson does not deploy Front Door.

questions.stem: Which documented command reads endpoint priorities and monitor states?

optionExplanations.A: Destroy changes resources.
optionExplanations.C: The list operation reads endpoint metadata.

questions.stem: A plan unexpectedly changes the secondary target. What must be verified before apply?

options.B: Intended host, independence, and public HTTPS behavior

optionExplanations.A: File existence is not content review.
optionExplanations.C: Length does not establish service health.

questions.stem: DNS routing fails over. What happens to an already established client connection because of DNS alone?

options.A: Its TLS session transfers to the backup
options.C: It is not moved by the DNS decision

optionExplanations.A: There is no TLS-session proxy.
optionExplanations.B: Terraform does not own client sockets.
optionExplanations.C: Applications need their own reconnection behavior.
optionExplanations.D: DNS does not rewrite established connections.

questions.stem: A browser resolves a CNAME. Which host is normally used in its original HTTP Host header?

options.B: The hostname in the requested URL

optionExplanations.A: Resource addresses are not HTTP hosts.
optionExplanations.B: DNS aliases do not rewrite the requested URL.
optionExplanations.C: Subscription names do not set Host headers.
optionExplanations.D: Resolvers answer DNS, not application host selection.

questions.stem: A team wants /images and /checkout routed to different services. What is missing?

options.A: An application-layer router inspecting URL paths

optionExplanations.A: Traffic Manager cannot inspect HTTP request paths.
optionExplanations.C: Uniqueness does not add path routing.

questions.stem: An unsafe hostname is corrected after saving tfplan. What is the safe next step?

options.C: Apply the old plan and rely on checks
options.D: Generate and review a new plan

optionExplanations.A: Display text is not executable plan data.
optionExplanations.B: Saved plans retain their planned values.
optionExplanations.C: Checks do not rewrite saved plans.
optionExplanations.D: A new plan incorporates corrected inputs.

questions.stem: Resolve-DnsName returns a profile target. Which follow-up exercises the application?

options.A: Request the intended client URL and inspect the response

optionExplanations.A: The request tests connectivity, TLS, host routing, and response.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting checks source files.

questions.stem: After CLZ-330 destroy, which remaining check is documented?

options.B: Confirm az group exists returns false for the captured lesson group

optionExplanations.A: The lesson does not own all registrar state.
optionExplanations.B: Readback checks this lesson's resource-group absence.
optionExplanations.C: Applications are separately owned.
